rows.name_override: Signed Employment Contract — Norwegian Law Compliant
rows.description_override: Obtain a signed employment contract from the Norwegian employer before initiating any registration. The contract must comply with the Norwegian Working Environment Act (arbeidsmiljøloven) and include: position title, workplace, salary, hours, notice period, and start date.
rows.deadline_notes: Must be signed and in hand at least 7 days before the move date. Required as supporting document for police registration and D-number application.

rows.description_override: Register your right of residence with the local Norwegian police district. Bring passport, employment contract, and proof of accommodation. You will receive a registration certificate (registreringsbevis) which proves your legal right to reside and work in Norway.

conditions.description: Only mandatory if the planned stay exceeds 3 months

rows.deadline_notes: Must be completed within 90 days of arrival in Norway if the stay will exceed 3 months. Apply as early as possible — appointment slots at busy police stations can be several weeks out.

rows.description_override: Apply for a D-number (temporary Norwegian tax identification number) from Skatteetaten. Required for all non-resident workers in Norway. The D-number is a prerequisite for obtaining a tax card and opening a bank account. Applications can be made in person at a tax office or through some employers.
rows.deadline_notes: Apply immediately upon or before arrival — ideally before the first paycheck date. The D-number application can take 1-2 weeks to process. HR teams should initiate this simultaneously with relocation.

rows.description_override: Obtain a Norwegian tax card (skattekort) from Skatteetaten immediately after receiving your D-number. Submit the application online at skatteetaten.no. The employer will automatically receive the tax card digitally and apply the correct withholding rate to your salary.
rows.deadline_notes: Apply within 3 days of receiving D-number confirmation. The tax card must be in the employer's system before the first paycheck date. Employer must withhold 50% without it — recovery is possible but administratively burdensome.

rows.description_override: Open a NOK bank account at a Norwegian bank. Most Norwegian banks require a D-number for non-residents. Recommended banks with English-language services: DNB, Nordea, Handelsbanken. Some banks allow pre-arrival appointment booking.
rows.deadline_notes: Apply within 14 days of receiving D-number. Required to receive salary payments. Some banks have 2-4 week waiting lists for account opening appointments.

rows.description_override: If staying in Norway for more than 6 months, register as a resident in the Norwegian National Registry (Folkeregisteret). This replaces your D-number with a permanent 11-digit Norwegian national identity number (fødselsnummer / personnummer). Registration is done through Skatteetaten offices.

conditions.description: Only required if staying 6 months or more (183 days)

rows.deadline_notes: Must register within 8 weeks (56 days) of the 6-month mark of residence in Norway. Bring: passport, registration certificate from police, employment contract, and proof of Norwegian address.
